subject.title: fix(openshell): mirror sandboxes can modify workspace skill files despite read-only policy

question: Should OpenShell mirror mode enforce the same immutable existing-skill-root policy as Docker and the remote filesystem bridge, including discarding downloaded edits under those roots?
rationale: The patch is a narrow implementation of an established sibling policy, but it changes an execution-boundary guarantee and the external OpenShell mirror-download behavior has not been demonstrated against a live service endpoint.

options.title: Accept mirror-policy parity
options.body: Merge after rebase and CI refresh, treating existing `skills` and `.agents/skills` directories as owner-controlled and non-writable in OpenShell mirror mode.

options.title: Require live OpenShell proof first
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require a redacted real OpenShell mirror run that shows a sandbox-side skill edit cannot return to the host workspace.

recommendation.title: Accept mirror-policy parity
recommendation.body: Merge after rebase and CI refresh, treating existing `skills` and `.agents/skills` directories as owner-controlled and non-writable in OpenShell mirror mode.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged sandbox-skill materialization and read-only-boundary work that the PR explicitly extends.
